top.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt. top.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
top.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. top.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
top.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. top.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
top.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. top.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
top.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. top.title: Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong shares classy message after beating Shohei Ohtani for NL MVP
top.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong shares classy message after beating Shohei Ohtani for NL MVP appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Pete Crow-Armstrong may have dethroned Shohei Ohtani in the National League MVP race , but the Chicago Cubs star made sure to give the Los Angeles Dodgers superstar his due. Crow-Armstrong was named the unanimous winner of the 2026 NL MVP award on Thursday, with Ohtani finishing second after winning the honor in each of the last two seasons. Speaking on MLB Network after the announcement, the 24-year-old reflected on being mentioned in the same breath as the two-way star. “Being mentioned in conversations with, you know, one of the best pitchers in the sport, but also one of the best hitters, a World Series champion, and arguably the biggest part of that,” Crow-Armstrong said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "Being mentioned in conversations with one of the best pitchers in the sport who's also one of the best hitters… I want to be better than I was the day before." – @Cubs superstar Pete Crow-Armstrong on his NL MVP race with Shohei Ohtani and how he strived to improve in 2026 https://t.co/jEgUw4wJeH pic.twitter.com/AT3HYD77ZR — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) November 13, 2026 “It’s not like we’re racing and going up against each other every day. But I think it’s just the fact that I want to be better than I was the day before. And really, that’s been all that I’ve needed to motivate myself with for really as long as I can remember.” That drive showed up all season long. Crow-Armstrong played in all 162 games and led the NL in home runs (45), OPS (.943) and WAR (9.8), while also swiping 41 bases to join the 40-40 club . The two-time MLB All-Star also credited the people around him in the Cubs clubhouse, including manager Craig Counsell and teammates Alex Bregman and Nico Hoerner. “I’ve been lucky to be in really good clubhouses my first, you know, parts of four seasons up here. They give me patience and a lot of runway to be myself and succeed that way,” he said. Crow-Armstrong now joins a list of Cubs MVPs that includes Ernie Banks, Ryne Sandberg, Andre Dawson, Sammy Sosa and Kris Bryant. He singled out the late Sandberg, who supported him while battling cancer . “He made himself available for a lot of us over the last few years through chemo and everything. He was hugely important to the last few years of my life,” Crow-Armstrong said. He added that he had spoken with Bryant earlier in the day . “I’m happy to carry on their legacy,” he said. top.title: J.B. Bickerstaff Calls Out Pistons’ Terrible Defense After Cade Cunningham’s Historic 52-Point Game
top.description: DETROIT, MI - FEBRUARY 25: Cade Cunningham #2 and Head Coach J.B. Bickerstaff of the Detroit Pistons look on during the game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on February 25, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Brian Sevald/NBAE via Getty Images) Cade Cunningham led the Detroit Pistons to a 144-140 win over the Washington Wizards tonight with a historic 50+ point game. He finished with 52 points, 11 assists, five rebounds, one steal, and one block, shooting 16-25 from the field (64.0% FG) and 3-5 from beyond the arc (60.0% 3P). Cunningham is now the only player in NBA history to have 50+ points and 10+ assists with zero turnovers in a single game. After the game, head coach J.B. Bickerstaff praised Cade Cunningham’s leadership on offense but did not seem pleased that the Pistons allowed the Wizards to score 140 points. “It speaks to who he is; the more you’re around him, the more you respect him for who he is and what his abilities are. To be able to do what he does when the moment gets called on, it’s unique, and it’s special. He never ceases to amaze. He just understands what it takes to get it done and has all the abilities to make those things happen,” Bickerstaff said initially. “The efficiency of it, taking care of the ball, sharing the ball. The ball is in his hands so much versus so many different covers and actions against him, but I thought he just made the right play over and over again,” Bickerstaff later added on Cunningham’s zero turnovers tonight. A reporter then asked the Pistons’ head coach what he thought about the team’s resiliency in a double overtime win tonight. “I told the guys I was proud of their resolve; I respect their resolve,” he said. “But we made too many mistakes to put ourselves in that position. We hold ourselves to a higher standard. In certain moments, we have to be able to generate a stop; we’ve got to be able to trust each other. Tonight I thought we made too many mistakes in those moments.” “We didn’t pay attention to the details,” he added about allowing Trae Young to make the buzzer-beating three-point shot to tie the game in regulation. “It was bad. It was terrible. We were not up to our standard defensively,” he later added. “Everything was bad.” There is a reason why the Pistons are currently one of the best defenses in the league, with the second-best defensive rating right now (107.9), just inches behind the Celtics (107.6). Despite witnessing a historic offensive performance, J.B. Bickerstaff demands perfection on both ends of the floor from his team. So that reaction seems justifiable. The Pistons have now improved to 8-3 for the season and are third in the Eastern Conference. They now move on to face the Heat on Saturday, November 14. That will be a clash of two defensive powerhouses. It will certainly be interesting to see what adjustments J.B. Bickerstaff makes to their defensive strategies.

top.title: Cheating, scandal and drama - Wales agony v All Blacks
top.description: Martyn Williams admitted the famous haka stand-off was a "surreal" moment [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Cheating, national scandal, timekeeping disasters and spine-tingling drama... Wales against New Zealand rarely disappoints. The history of matches between two nations that bleed rugby - and plenty of the red stuff has been spilled over the years - is almost a history of the game itself. Since the 1905 'Match of the Century' which gave rise to the tradition of singing national anthems before sports events, they have battled. Wales may have won three of the first four meetings but since success in 1953 the lengthening losing run has hung like a millstone around the necks of generations of players. Gareth Edwards, Barry John, JPR Williams, Jonathan Davies, Shane Williams and Alun Wyn Jones all tried with Wales and failed. There is bitterness that the wait has gone on so long - more than 70 years - not least after one of the most talked about accusations of cheating in rugby history. Cardiff in 1978 hosted what was as close to a World Cup final as the time allowed. The All Blacks had defeated the British & Irish Lions the previous year and Wales were Grand Slam champions. It was the first time New Zealand had visited Cardiff since the infamous late-night incident which saw Keith Murdoch sent home in disgrace after punching a hotel doorman. Still today, All Blacks players, staff and fans stop at the Angel Hotel, opposite the Principality Stadium on Westgate Street, for a commemorative pint. Keith Murdoch became a recluse in Australia up until his death in 2018 [Getty Images] In 1978, Graham Mourie's tourists scored the game's only try but Wales had dominated, leading 12-10 as the clock inside the cauldron of the old Arms Park ticked towards the final minute. Little did they know that New Zealand's players, braced for their biggest challenge of the tour, had hatched an escape plan the previous night. Andy Haden, the All Blacks lock and culprit in chief, later wrote: "With Wales in front, I knew there could only be a minute or so left. I went to Frank Oliver, my locking partner... and told him the plan in four words: 'I'm going to dive'." Sure enough, Haden catapulted out of the line-out just as Wales hooker Bobby Windsor threw the ball. Wales' players stood bemused as referee Roger Quittenton of England gave a penalty and Brian McKechnie landed the winning points. Quittenton would later claim he had penalised Geoff Wheel for an infringement, but the Kiwi intent was clear and the apparent injustice would rankle. Andy Haden later admitted in his autobiography that the All Blacks hatched a plan to cheat [Colorsport/Shutterstock] Windsor described the game as the worst day of his career. He added: "I knew straight away that it was a con job. When we found out later that they had planned it the night before, that really got to me. I'll never forget that as long as I live." top.title: Commanders beat Giants 24-21 with late Diggs touchdown
top.description: Stefon Diggs evaded two tackles and dashed to the line before turning and dramatically falling backward into the end zone (Emilee Chinn) Stefon Diggs' late touchdown secured a tense 24-21 Washington Commanders win over the New York Giants after Cam Skattebo had rushed for two touchdowns Thursday. Commanders QB Jayden Daniels, who had not thrown an interception all season, threw two on consecutive drives while seeking a comeback in a wild fourth quarter, before finding veteran receiver Diggs with a minute remaining for the go-ahead touchdown. Daniels finished with 249 passing yards and three TDs, with Antonio Williams and Ben Sinnott also reaching the end zone for Washington. Giants signal-caller JJ McCarthy threw for 293 yards and a touchdown to Isaiah Likely, with his veteran backup Jameis Winston also taking to the field for several valuable quarterback sneaks. The late loss prevented New York pulling clear in the NFC East, with the Giants remaining top on 5-3-1 but closely trailed by the Dallas Cowboys (4-5) and Washington, who moved to 3-5-1. "We came out here a little shaky, we had some execution problems here and there, but we cleaned it up and we saw what kind of team we could be," said Diggs. top.description: Gerome Warburton has won 18 of his 22 professional fights [Getty Images] Welsh boxer Gerome Warburton says facing world champion Carlos Adames will complete his boxing journey as he looks to prove he belongs at the top level. The 31-year-old will face WBC middleweight champion Adames, 32, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday, 14 November, though the world title is not on the line. The WBA continental champion is not ranked by the WBC, and will instead face once-beaten Adames at super middleweight in a non-title main event. Warburton, from Colwyn Bay, believes he has earned this career-defining shot after years of overcoming the odds on the British scene. "You're in there to do a job. This is a big hurdle to get over, but I've been jumping over hurdles my whole career." The 5ft 11in (1.8m) former Welsh middleweight champion added: "This is another occasion to prove wrong those people who think I can't achieve something. Jaylen Brown is hoping the 7-foot-6 center can get some more playing time moving forward . “We need some more tall people. The duo, who spoke while addressing party faithful and mmmoth crowd, at the Lagos All Progressives Congress, APC, East Senatorial District Rally, held on Thursday, at the Epe Recreational Ground, Epe, said President Tinubu had laid a solid foundation for Lagos State over two decades ago, providing the blueprint for the state’s sustained growth and development. nigeria.title: Spain beat Czech Republic to retain perfect Nations League record
nigeria.description: Alex Baena scored from the spot and Marc Pubill added another seconds from time as Spain beat ten-men Czech Republic 2-0 in the Nations League in Prague on Thursday. The win leaves Spain unbeaten in 44 competitive games in a row, including five wins in as many Nations League games this season. Spain, who already secured a quarter-final berth before travelling to Prague, will face England in Madrid on Sunday in their final Group A3 game. Baena scored on 39 minutes after a VAR check revealed Czech midfielder Lukas Ambros had handled the ball inside the box. The Atletico Madrid winger blasted his spot kick past Matej Kovar who touched the ball but failed to clear it. Czech captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off in the 69th minute after bringing down second-half substitute Roberto Fernandez on a counter-attack. It was a deja-vu for the Wolverhampton defender who also got a red card at the end of Spain’s 3-1 home win over the Czechs last month. Pubill, another substitute, beat Kovar with a low shot deep into stoppage time after the Czech back four left him alone facing the Eindhoven goalkeeper. Luis de la Fuentes missed Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Rodri and Eric Garcia over injuries while Mikel Oyarzabal was sidelined with flu for the Prague game. Spain got off to a slow start on the chilly evening but never really let the hosts get close throughout the first half. They gradually stepped up their pressure, often confining the Czechs to their box and looking for chances. Fabian Ruiz hit the post with a curling right-footer three minutes from halftime, while Dean Huijsen’s header found Kovar’s arms. Yeremy Pino, replacing Yamal on the right flank, saw his goal overturned by VAR for offside just two minutes into the second half. The Czechs showed higher spirits after the break, but David Zima tipped the ball over the bar from close range on 50 minutes and Adam Hlozek’s glancing header landed on the top of the crossbar. The Czechs lost momentum after the red card, but Baena had two efforts cleared by Kovar who also denied Fernandez from close range. The hosts, led by de la Fuente’s long-time collaborator Santi Denia, have lost all their Nations League games this season. They are next travelling to Croatia for a game they need to win to stay in the top tier of the competititon for the next edition. nigeria.title: Record-breaking Kane fires England into Nations League knockouts
nigeria.description: Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England appearance with a goal from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 on Thursday to book a place in the Nations League quarter-finals. Slaven Bilic’s team were determined to avoid the embarrassment of their 7-0 mauling by England in Rijeka last month and looked much more solid from the kick-off. But goals from Morgan Rogers and captain Kane kept England second in their group, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March. Neither side got out of second gear in the opening stages of the match at Wembley. Elliot Anderson fired over in the 16th minute and Croatia’s Josip Misic flashed a shot wide midway through the first half. Chelsea forward Rogers broke the deadlock in the 24th minute in slightly fortuitous fashion following a neat move by the home side. Kane floated a ball to Jude Bellingham on the right of the penalty area and the Real Madrid man cushioned the ball first time across the area towards Rogers. Manchester City’s Josko Gvardiol had a chance to clear but got in a tangle and Chelsea’s Rogers poked the ball past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic. England started to find some rhythm as they went in search of a second goal but failed to add to their tally before half-time. Thomas Tuchel’s men were again the more potent team at the beginning of the second period. But the visitors levelled against the run of play just before the hour mark after a glaring error by England defender Jarell Quansah, who misdirected a header from close range towards Jordan Pickford following a Croatia corner. The ball fell to Petar Sucic, who stabbed home. Minutes later England were back in front, with Bayer Leverkusen defender Quansah again at the heart of the action after his shirt was tugged in the penalty area. Referee Morten Krogh initially did not award a penalty but he was sent to the monitor by the VAR and pointed to the spot. Kane made no mistake, drilling home for record-extending 92nd England goal. Nikola Vlasic gave England a scare, firing just wide of Jordan Pickford’s goal as Croatia showed they were still alive. James Garner thought he had scored a third for England after a Bellingham cut-back but Bellingham was in an off-side position when he received the ball. Ballon d’Or winner Kane won his 126th cap when the game kicked off — taking him clear of his tie with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton. A giant banner was raised before kick-off with a picture of the 33-year-old and the words “England’s Finest”. Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions skipper, along with Football Association patron Prince William. England remain second in Nations League Group A3, after leaders Spain beat the Czech Republic 2-0 but are now assured of a place in the quarter-finals. nigeria.title: Online safety concerns are reshaping how people meet strangers
nigeria.description: It’s hard to ignore how meeting new people online has changed in the past decade. With so many platforms connecting millions, the possibilities feel endless, but the risks have become more visible too. Stories about scams, harassment, and data breaches are everywhere, and they’ve made people think twice before reaching out to someone they don’t know. Safety concerns aren’t just in the background anymore—they’re shaping the way we start conversations, choose platforms, and decide how much to share. As awareness grows, so do new habits and expectations for digital introductions. This shift doesn’t just affect individuals; it’s influencing whole communities as we all adapt to a more cautious, connected world. Changing first steps: why some users now engage with strangers differently online That growing caution is easy to spot in the way people now approach first interactions with strangers online. Instead of jumping right into open conversations, many start by looking for platforms that let them control who they talk to, or give them the option to remain anonymous until they feel comfortable. Features like one-click exit buttons, video previews, or private chat rooms have become popular for exactly this reason. Women, in particular, are leading this change. They’re more likely to say safety is a top concern, which shows up in everything from avoiding certain apps to using aliases or insisting on in-app messaging only. The choice of platform matters too. Video chat sites, for example, offer a sense of control because users can see and hear who they’re talking to—and can leave the conversation instantly if something doesn’t feel right. For many, getting to know LuckyCrush and similar services is part of this shift toward safer, more controlled first steps when meeting someone new. It’s a sign that concerns are not stopping people from connecting, but are changing the rules for how those first moments happen. a shift in trust: navigating caution in the age of digital introductions That change in first steps is really about trust—how it’s built, how it’s lost, and why it matters so much now. People aren’t just jumping into conversations and sharing details the way they might have a decade ago. Instead, there’s this sense of needing to pause and check for warning signs. With more stories surfacing about online fraud and harassment, it feels riskier to let your guard down. A lot of users now watch for inconsistent stories, pressure to move chats off-platform, or requests for private information as red flags that something isn’t right. Some of the ways people protect themselves include sticking to messaging within the app, looking for verification badges, or even googling someone before agreeing to meet. nigeria.title: UNN Deaths: Gov Mbah mourns, orders investigation
nigeria.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr Peter Mbah, has expressed deep grief over the deaths of four students of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, who reportedly died during an off-campus sign-out party organised for one of their friends, describing the incident as a heartbreaking loss. Mbah described the deaths as a grievous loss, not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to Enugu State as a whole. He called for a ban on sign-out parties among undergraduates, noting that the practice had brought too much sorrow to families and tertiary institutions across the country. This was contained in a press statement issued by the governor’s media aide, Mazi Uche Anichukwu, on Thursday. “I received with rude shock and deep sense of loss the news of the off-campus sign-out party leading to the death of four students of the University of Nigeria Nsukka, and hospitalisation of six others. “This is a grievous loss not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to us as a state. Losing them in their prime and along with their promising future cuts as deeply as a sharp knife. We, therefore share in this grief and pray God to grant their families, friends, and the UNN community the equanimity to bear the heartbreaking loss. “Our hearts go out to their parents in particular, who sacrificed personal comforts to sponsor their children through the university, but only to face this sad turn of events. “As a government, we have ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding their deaths and will work closely with the university authorities and security agencies to get to the roots of the sad development and forestall a recurrence. “In the meantime, I have suspended my scheduled town hall meeting with the UNN community on Friday, November 13, 2026, as we join the university in mourning the dead. “Going forward, we will work with the authorities of tertiary institutions to enforce a full ban on sign-out parties and other excessive celebrations, a trend that has cost more lives and brought more sorrows than joy to families and higher institutions of learning,” the governor stated. Mbah also called for increased public enlightenment campaigns by relevant agencies and institutions on the consequences of drug use and abuse. nigeria.title: My Ambition Is To Ensure Tinubu’s 2027 Victory, Says Matawalle
nigeria.description: The Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, says his major ambition is to ensure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. Matawalle made this known while addressing supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) at his residence in Gusau, Zamfara State, ahead of the expected visit of the First Lady, Senator Remi Tinubu. He urged party members to unite and intensify mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election, as well as the victory of other APC candidates in the state. The minister commended Tinubu’s efforts in tackling insecurity, developing infrastructure and promoting political cohesion, expressing his commitment to ensuring that the President completes his eight-year tenure. Matawalle said that after discharging his responsibilities as Minister of State for Defence, particularly in the fight against insecurity, his next major priority would be to work towards Tinubu’s re-election. He also dismissed what he described as provocations and propaganda by individuals seeking to tarnish his image, insisting that his priority was to sustain unity within the APC in Zamfara and secure victories for the party at all levels. The minister further dismissed allegations and propaganda concerning Tinubu’s health, maintaining that the President was fit to continue providing leadership and direction for the country. On security, Matawalle assured Zamfara residents that the Federal Government would deploy additional security personnel along major highways to protect commuters from persistent bandit attacks. He specifically mentioned the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway, as well as the Gummi-Anka-Bukkuyum and Tsafe access roads, as routes that would receive increased security attention. “We will deploy security forces along the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway to ensure the safe movement of commuters. We will also deploy security personnel to ensure the safety of those travelling along the Gummi, Anka, Bukkuyum and Tsafe roads,” he said. Matawalle pledged to do everything within his capacity to address insecurity in Zamfara and other parts of the country. He also spoke on the controversy surrounding the rerun election in Zamfara North Senatorial District, dismissing allegations of attempts to undermine his political standing and create divisions within the APC. The minister questioned the rationale behind the violence reportedly recorded during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji, insisting that political disagreements should not lead to attacks or destruction. “Those who caused the crisis during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji know whether they can emerge victorious or not. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Wins Court Authority to Seize $1.2 Billion of North Korea’s Stolen Binance Crypto as Freezes Top $2.7 Billion The DOJ said Thursday it has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance, part of a freeze of more than $2.7 billion that officials said halted about half of North Korea’s October exchange heist. In a Thursday announcement, the department said that on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as TraderTraitor, stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from Binance. That is below the $6.34 billion figure Binance has covered since the attack. Binance said it had completed coverage of the assets hit in the breach, replacing the tokens from company funds rather than by recovering the stolen coins. Those are separate tracks: the DOJ is trying to interdict what was taken, while the exchange has said users were made whole from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its treasury. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the DOJ’s Criminal Division said the department and its partners were able to “immediately halt about half of this historic breach” by freezing stolen assets “before they got beyond law enforcement reach.” The freeze of more than $2.7 billion is a joint figure for U.S. government and private-sector efforts. Of that amount, the DOJ said it has already obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion. The underlying court papers were not posted with the announcement. The $1.2 billion is not newly recovered money but comes out of the roughly $2.85 billion Binance said on Nov. 3 had been frozen or intercepted, and Thursday’s court authorization is the legal step that lets the government move toward taking ownership of those funds through forfeiture, where until now they had simply been frozen at the token issuers. Even that freeze is not the end of the trail. The DOJ said TraderTraitor actors are still moving the stolen assets through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges, and that tracing, seizure and forfeiture work continues. Last week, on Oct. 31, the FBI, with the U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, issued a Cyber Alert attributing the theft to North Korea and urging virtual asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses the actors are using. The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services. The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms. Neither the Justice Department nor Europol split the $234 million between cash and cryptocurrency, and neither named bitcoin or any other coin in the official totals. Europol put the European share at more than €60 million in cash and cryptocurrencies, alongside 950 kilograms of drugs and 57 firearms, and the U.S. share at more than €150 million, or $166 million, in cash and cryptocurrencies, plus more than 4.8 metric tons of drugs and 152 firearms. Those regional money figures still combine cash and crypto. Europol said its forensic and blockchain analysis teams traced illicit transactions as part of the work. business.description: ▶ Bitcoin Magazine Peter Schiff on the Bitcoin Crash: “Get the Hell Out” Challenged on why two or three down years would matter for Bitcoin when gold and the Nasdaq have had similar streaks before recoveries, Peter Schiff says the difference is the backdrop. When a market can’t go up on the best news it has ever had, he argues, that normally indicates that it’s going to go down. He calls Bitcoin “all hype,” with no intrinsic value, income, or dividends, and says much of the supply now sits with ETF investors and Bitcoin treasury companies rather than people who want to use it as money. All of that hot money, he warns, is going to exit, the market will go down faster than it went up, and he expects a massive washout. Even long-term bulls, he says, will have cheaper opportunities after leveraged speculators are cleared out, and he adds that this is not the time to be hodling. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. entertainment.description: With NTDA leading the national delegation, NTT Global Destinations mobilising international partnerships and diaspora networks, and NANTA representing Nigeria’s private tourism sector, the Nigeria Pavilion became a vibrant celebration of culture, community and tourism opportunities. For three exciting days, Nigeria brought its rhythm, culture, hospitality and entrepreneurial spirit to the global stage at World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, held from 3 to 5 November at ExCeL London. Supporting the national showcase was NTT Global Destinations (NGD), NTDA’s Strategic and Pavilion Implementation Partner, responsible for coordinating the exhibition’s planning, stakeholder engagement, international liaison and delivery. From the energetic rhythms to conversations about Nigeria’s tourism offering, the pavilion quickly became a gathering point for visitors interested in discovering more about the country. Among the highlights was the opportunity to connect Nigerian culture with the global appeal of Nollywood, Afrobeats and contemporary African creativity. The Director General Who Stole the Show Perhaps one of the most memorable moments came when NTDA Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, joined the traditional drummers and dancers in an energetic cultural performance. Rather than remaining a spectator, the DG became part of the attraction, embracing the rhythm and excitement of the Nigerian showcase. His performance drew attention and captured the spirit of the exhibition: a country confidently presenting its culture to the world. It was tourism diplomacy in its most authentic form, demonstrating that sometimes the most powerful way to promote a destination is simply to experience and celebrate it. Held from October 16 to 23, 2026, the week-long festival took cocktail culture beyond borders, bringing together some of the most exciting talents and bar communities from Lagos, Accra, and Abidjan. At the heart of this year’s celebration was a powerful message: Africa’s cocktail industry thrives when creativity, culture, and expertise flow freely across borders. The celebrations took off on Sunday, October 18, as the Italian Trade Agency brought a touch of Italian sophistication to the festival with the Italian Cocktail Experience, an exclusive, invitation-only masterclass and Aperitivo Italiano held at Mr Panther, Victoria Island. The experience offered guests an opportunity to explore the artistry and traditions of Italian cocktail culture. Speaking at the event, Maurizio Ferri , Director of the Italian Trade Agency, highlighted the initiative’s goal of promoting Italian wines and spirits, featuring brands such as Campari, Aperol and Martini. The experience began with a masterclass hosted by Lara Rawa , founder of Lagos Cocktail Week, exploring five Italian classics: the Negroni, Americano, Bellini, Aperol Spritz and Garibaldi. Guests learned about the Italian aperitif tradition and how individual palates shape cocktail preferences. The evening continued with networking, Italian wine and cocktail tastings, and special guests, including Chef Gibbs and visiting bartenders from Abidjan and Ghana. With music by DJ Exclusive , the event combined cultural exchange, education and entertainment in celebration of Italian cocktail culture. entertainment.title: Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List
entertainment.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram If Olamide ‘s ‘ Burukutu ‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space . Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project. Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu . Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range. The newly revealed tracklist opens with “ Elohim ” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “ Skoskola “, “ Say Less “, the lead anthem “ Burukutu “, and “ Alujon ” rounding out the first half. The second half picks up the tempo with “ Mbiri “, the collaborative track “ Jaiye ” featuring vocalist Fola , followed by “ Oshey “, “ Ring “, and the closing record “ Jogor “. Keeping features remarkably streamlined, the album highlights a targeted guest appearance from Nigerian singer Fola, allowing Olamide’s distinctive penmanship and vocal direction to take centre stage across the entire tracklist. The official 10-track tracklist for Olamide’s album Time & Space, featuring lead single Burukutu and a guest appearance by Fola. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram This forthcoming release arrives as the direct successor to his self-titled studio album, Olamidé , which dropped in June 2025 with a sprawling 17-track setup featuring heavyweights like Wizkid . Where that previous body of work leaned into massive collaborative constellations, Time & Space scales back into a more intimate, focused exploration of sound, anchored tightly by the creative vision of the YBNL boss himself. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. sports.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
sports.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. sports.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
sports.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They’re confident they can challenge any defense vertically. “The underneath throws are going to be there,” Hampton said. “We got the best OC in the country; we’re going to be able to go deep if we want to.” Latest Beavers news Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson going through further testing of hand injury before Boise State game Oregon State basketball lands 3-star center for 2027 class Oregon State wome

Pete Crow-Armstrong may have dethroned Shohei Ohtani in the National League MVP race , but the Chicago Cubs star made sure to give the Los Angeles Dodgers superstar his due. Crow-Armstrong was named the unanimous winner of the 2026 NL MVP award on Thursday, with Ohtani finishing second after winning the honor in each of the last two seasons. Speaking on MLB Network after the announcement, the 24-year-old reflected on being mentioned in the same breath as the two-way star. “Being mentioned in conversations with, you know, one of the best pitchers in the sport, but also one of the best hitters, a World Series champion, and arguably the biggest part of that,” Crow-Armstrong said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "Being mentioned in conversations with one of the best pitchers in the sport who's also one of the best hitters… I want to be better than I was the day before." – @Cubs superstar Pete Crow-Armstrong on his NL MVP race with Shohei Ohtani and how he strived to improve in 2026 https://t.co/jEgUw4wJeH pic.twitter.com/AT3HYD77ZR — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) November 13, 2026 “It’s not like we’re racing and going up against each other every day. But I think it’s just the fact that I want to be better than I was the day before. And really, that’s been all that I’ve needed to motivate myself with for really as long as I can remember.” That drive showed up all season long. Crow-Armstrong played in all 162 games and led the NL in home runs (45), OPS (.943) and WAR (9.8), while also swiping 41 bases to join the 40-40 club . The two-time MLB All-Star also credited the people around him in the Cubs clubhouse, including manager Craig Counsell and teammates Alex Bregman and Nico Hoerner. “I’ve been lucky to be in really good clubhouses my first, you know, parts of four seasons up here. They give me patience and a lot of runway to be myself and succeed that way,” he said. Crow-Armstrong now joins a list of Cubs MVPs that includes Ernie Banks, Ryne Sandberg, Andre Dawson, Sammy Sosa and Kris Bryant. He singled out the late Sandberg, who supported him while battling cancer . “He made himself available for a lot of us over the last few years through chemo and everything. He was hugely important to the last few years of my life,” Crow-Armstrong said. He added that he had spoken with Bryant earlier in the day . “I’m happy to carry on their legacy,” he said. sports.title: J.B. Bickerstaff Calls Out Pistons’ Terrible Defense After Cade Cunningham’s Historic 52-Point Game
sports.description: DETROIT, MI - FEBRUARY 25: Cade Cunningham #2 and Head Coach J.B. Bickerstaff of the Detroit Pistons look on during the game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on February 25, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Brian Sevald/NBAE via Getty Images) Cade Cunningham led the Detroit Pistons to a 144-140 win over the Washington Wizards tonight with a historic 50+ point game. He finished with 52 points, 11 assists, five rebounds, one steal, and one block, shooting 16-25 from the field (64.0% FG) and 3-5 from beyond the arc (60.0% 3P). Cunningham is now the only player in NBA history to have 50+ points and 10+ assists with zero turnovers in a single game. After the game, head coach J.B. Bickerstaff praised Cade Cunningham’s leadership on offense but did not seem pleased that the Pistons allowed the Wizards to score 140 points. “It speaks to who he is; the more you’re around him, the more you respect him for who he is and what his abilities are. To be able to do what he does when the moment gets called on, it’s unique, and it’s special. He never ceases to amaze. He just understands what it takes to get it done and has all the abilities to make those things happen,” Bickerstaff said initially. “The efficiency of it, taking care of the ball, sharing the ball. The ball is in his hands so much versus so many different covers and actions against him, but I thought he just made the right play over and over again,” Bickerstaff later added on Cunningham’s zero turnovers tonight. A reporter then asked the Pistons’ head coach what he thought about the team’s resiliency in a double overtime win tonight. “I told the guys I was proud of their resolve; I respect their resolve,” he said. “But we made too many mistakes to put ourselves in that position. We hold ourselves to a higher standard. In certain moments, we have to be able to generate a stop; we’ve got to be able to trust each other. Tonight I thought we made too many mistakes in those moments.” “We didn’t pay attention to the details,” he added about allowing Trae Young to make the buzzer-beating three-point shot to tie the game in regulation. “It was bad. It was terrible. We were not up to our standard defensively,” he later added. “Everything was bad.” There is a reason why the Pistons are currently one of the best defenses in the league, with the second-best defensive rating right now (107.9), just inches behind the Celtics (107.6). Despite witnessing a historic offensive performance, J.B. Bickerstaff demands perfection on both ends of the floor from his team. So that reaction seems justifiable. The Pistons have now improved to 8-3 for the season and are third in the Eastern Conference. They now move on to face the Heat on Saturday, November 14. That will be a clash of two defensive powerhouses. It will certainly be interesting to see what adjustments J.B. Bickerstaff makes to their defensive strategies.

sports.description: Martyn Williams admitted the famous haka stand-off was a "surreal" moment [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Cheating, national scandal, timekeeping disasters and spine-tingling drama... Wales against New Zealand rarely disappoints. The history of matches between two nations that bleed rugby - and plenty of the red stuff has been spilled over the years - is almost a history of the game itself. Since the 1905 'Match of the Century' which gave rise to the tradition of singing national anthems before sports events, they have battled. Wales may have won three of the first four meetings but since success in 1953 the lengthening losing run has hung like a millstone around the necks of generations of players. Gareth Edwards, Barry John, JPR Williams, Jonathan Davies, Shane Williams and Alun Wyn Jones all tried with Wales and failed. There is bitterness that the wait has gone on so long - more than 70 years - not least after one of the most talked about accusations of cheating in rugby history. Cardiff in 1978 hosted what was as close to a World Cup final as the time allowed. The All Blacks had defeated the British & Irish Lions the previous year and Wales were Grand Slam champions. It was the first time New Zealand had visited Cardiff since the infamous late-night incident which saw Keith Murdoch sent home in disgrace after punching a hotel doorman. Still today, All Blacks players, staff and fans stop at the Angel Hotel, opposite the Principality Stadium on Westgate Street, for a commemorative pint. Keith Murdoch became a recluse in Australia up until his death in 2018 [Getty Images] In 1978, Graham Mourie's tourists scored the game's only try but Wales had dominated, leading 12-10 as the clock inside the cauldron of the old Arms Park ticked towards the final minute. Little did they know that New Zealand's players, braced for their biggest challenge of the tour, had hatched an escape plan the previous night. Andy Haden, the All Blacks lock and culprit in chief, later wrote: "With Wales in front, I knew there could only be a minute or so left. I went to Frank Oliver, my locking partner... and told him the plan in four words: 'I'm going to dive'." Sure enough, Haden catapulted out of the line-out just as Wales hooker Bobby Windsor threw the ball. Wales' players stood bemused as referee Roger Quittenton of England gave a penalty and Brian McKechnie landed the winning points. Quittenton would later claim he had penalised Geoff Wheel for an infringement, but the Kiwi intent was clear and the apparent injustice would rankle. He added: "I knew straight away that it was a con job. When we found out later that they had planned it the night before, that really got to me. I'll never forget that as long as I live." Game No. 20 brought a new set of challenges, as both Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar exited Thursday night’s eventual 4-3 overtime loss to the Ottawa Senators with lower-body injuries. Those two storylines have quickly jumped to the top of the list of concerns for a team that was slowly starting to figure things out. There’s a chance Colorado could have to play without both of them, but we won’t know more until Saturday. Basically, both guys could miss 12 days of action, and it would only cost them three games. We’ll see what happens in Montreal. sports.title: Fletcher savors High School Gator Bowl football chance: 'One more time'
sports.description: One more chance in Fletcher purple and white. Maverick Mills made it count. "I was so excited when I found out we got one more game," the Fletcher senior said. "One more time to go out with the guys." With three touchdown catches from Mills, three takeaways on defense and nearly 300 combined rushing yards from Jah'myri (Grown Man) Jennings and Ja'mez Williams, Fletcher entered Northeast Florida's football records as the winner of the inaugural High School Gator Bowl , defeating Ribault 43-30 on Nov. 12 at Nimnicht Stadium inside Fort Family Regional Park. The game, which benefits Walk Off Charities' youth instructional programs, matched the two Gateway Conference schools after both missed out on the Florida High School Athletic Association regional playoffs. How to submit your high school sports highlights to the Times-Union Mills' three touchdown catches from Ty Keister helped Fletcher jump ahead 28-0, while Jennings (16 carries, 189 yards) and Williams (10 carries, 98 yards) controlled the tempo and Chase Durden also took a 44-yard end-around to the house. The Trojans (5-6) never even reached midfield in the first half, but they mounted a furious late comeback behind 263 passing yards and four touchdowns (three passing, one rushing) from quarterback Ashton Wiggins. But through a chaotic fourth quarter, which included three touchdowns in 56 seconds at one stage, Fletcher's defense came through when it counted. Junior Xavier Carmichael finished with four sacks of Wiggins and the Senators grabbed three interceptions, two by Dominic Smith. "I've got to keep using those swim moves and getting around that [blocking], man," Carmichael said. For the Senators (6-5), who fell short of the FHSAA playoffs in an unforgiving numbers game from Florida's bruising Region 1-5A, the High School Gator Bowl not only sends out the senior class on a winning note but also sets the stage for the next wave at the beach. Carmichael, Smith and running back Romelo Johnson are among the Fletcher players on course to return for 2027. "It's a blessing," Fletcher head coach Ciatrick Fason said. sports.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ — The New York Giants were in the NFC East driver's seat entering their "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Washington Commanders . The game turned from a boring, weather-effected affair into more pleasant conditions with better football. And in the end, it was the Commanders who made more plays. As always, there were winners and losers within the final result. Let's break it down. Winners Jayden Daniels The quarterback made plenty of plays, but the current version of this Commanders team needs him to be Superman to win. He missed Stefon Diggs on a crucial fourth down with nine minutes to play in regulation. He made up for it later. Daniels wants to win above all. Another loss, effectively ending the Commanders’ chances of contention in 2026 – although anything is possible in the NFL – would not sit well with the franchise QB who is eligible for an extension this offseason. The Washington quarterback did all he could to keep his team competitive despite being the less-talented roster, completing plays like a 30-yard strike to Diggs while rolling to his right and the 1-yard touchdown throw to tight end Ben Sinnott in the second quarter. Likely’s 66-yard touchdown gave the Giants a 21-17 lead, and he finished with 9 catches (11 targets) for 127 yards. sports.title: Bruins Make Sudden Jeremy Swayman Decision During Difficult Canadiens Game
sports.description: The Boston Bruins make a sudden Jeremy Swayman decision during a difficult game against the Montreal Canadiens. Find out what prompted the move. Getty Jeremy Swayman exited the Boston Bruins’ crease Thursday night after Montreal went up 4-0, with Michael DiPietro taking over in the second period. With the Bruins and Canadiens separated by a single point atop the Atlantic Division entering the night, was the switch based on Swayman’s performance, or was it a message to a team that showed up in lackadaisical fashion? Swayman surrendered four goals on 17 shots before coach Marco Sturm made the change. Kirby Dach put Montreal in front in the first period with a spinning move, and Josh Anderson doubled the lead by banging home a rebound for his eighth goal of the season. Jake Evans made it 3-0 in the second, breaking in alone after a Jacob Fowler save and beating Swayman with a soft shot through the pads. Cole Caufield followed on another breakaway, snapping a shot into the top of the net. Phillip Danault later beat DiPietro for a fifth, and Boston answered to make it 5-1. Swayman wasn’t on the Bruins’ pregame injury report, which listed only forward James Hagens (back), and nothing in the game coverage suggested he was hurt when DiPietro skated in. The numbers were rough. Swayman finished with a .765 save percentage, and two of the four goals came on breakaways. Still, Sturm has a record of pulling Swayman to send a signal, not to punish him. After a 5-4 loss at Detroit on Dec. 2, 2025, in which Swayman allowed five goals on 23 shots, the coach pointed at the skaters in front of him. “It was almost not fair the way we played in front of him,” Sturm said, according to WEEI . The move, he explained, was meant to jolt the group, not indict the goalie. He did it again in Game 4 of last spring’s first-round series against the Buffalo Sabres, pulling Swayman after he stopped 23 shots in a 6-1 loss. Swayman shouted down the bench on his way off the ice. “It was not his fault today, I can tell you that,” Sturm said afterward, according to WEEI . Thursday marked at least the sixth time Swayman has been pulled since the start of the 2024-25 season. The Detroit and Buffalo games came under Sturm. The earlier three were Oct. 31, 2024, against Carolina , Jan. 22, 2025, against New Jersey and March 13, 2025, against Ottawa . sports.title: Cade Cunningham did something no NBA star has ever managed in 52-point performance
sports.description: Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images Cade Cunningham had a monster performance in the Detroit Pistons win, and he made NBA history in the process. It has been a shaky start to the season for Cade Cunningham with the Detroit Pistons. The superstar point guard has put up a couple of fairly poor performances in some big games, including against the Los Angeles Lakers. However, he made sure no one will talk about them anymore with his Thursday night display. Cunningham went off in a double overtime, 144-140 win against the Washington Wizards. The 25-year-old had a whopping 52 points and 10 assists in the game. It would have been an impressive showing considering that it was a 52-point double-double, but one particular stat made it historic. Cade Cunningham became the first player ever to have 50 points and 10 assists with zero turnovers in a game Cade can be inefficient at times, his shooting comes and goes. However, the one thing he has always excelled at is his playmaking. Like any primary offensive creator, the Pistons man is prone to turning the ball over; that is just an occupational hazard. However, in his monster game against Washington, it didn’t happen even once. That means Cunningham just did something no one has before. “HISTORY FOR CADE! Cade Cunningham is the first player in NBA HISTORY with 50 points, 10 assists and 0 turnovers in a game since individual turnovers were first tracked in 1977-78,” ESPN shared in a post on social media. Cunningham can be inconsistent and that will lead to some criticism from time to time. However, he is one of the most talented stars in the league. On evenings like this, he has simply reminded his doubters that he is capable of a lot more than he is given credit for. sports.title: Frank Nazar Scores Twice, Ryan Donato Wins It For Blackhawks 3-2 Over Sabres In Overtime
sports.description: CHICAGO - The Chicago Blackhawks were back at the United Center for Thursday night hockey against the Buffalo Sabres. After a lousy road trip made for a noisy week around the organization, they finally hit the ice for a game. Buffalo was coming into this in a back-to-back situation, as they were beaten soundly (8-3) by the Tampa Bay Lightning on Wednesday. Of course, they had the attitude of a team that wanted to make it right, but there is also a disadvantage to playing the night prior with travel. This was the first time that the Blackhawks played since the prior Saturday. After being blown out 9-2 by the Carolina Hurricanes, it became an eventful week for Chicago. In addition to lots of practice, there was a backup goalie change, a vote of confidence for the head coach, and the GM spoke at a press conference. After all of that, there was pressure on the Blackhawks to play better. You can't always expect a win, but you can expect a good effort and not to be blown out. The first period was not great for Chicago. For the entire first half of the period, they were hemmed in to their own zone, which has become a tradition for them when they are playing playoff-caliber teams. It finally resulted in a goal for Buffalo at 9:00 in the opening frame. Owen Power gave his team a 1-0 lead with his 3rd of the season. Shockingly (based on their play), this 1-0 lead didn't last long for the Sabres. At 12:22 of the first, Frank Nazar tied it when Connor Bedard made a great centering pass for him to score on the power play. At 15:46, however, Tage Thompson gave the Sabres the lead back. Jack Quinn made a great play along the wall to find Thompson, who zipped one home. That 2-1 score would not only hold through the first intermission, but the second as well. The Sabres completely dominated play for most of the middle frame, but they were unable to beat Spencer Knight. In the third period, the Blackhawks looked like the team that was well rested, while the Sabres looked like the team that played in a difficult game the night prior. At 8:22 of the final frame, Sam Rinzel threw one on net, and Frank Nazar deflected it home to tie the game at 2. Towards the end of the regulation, the Sabres did find a little bit of energy and started to control play more. That momentum was killed by a penalty drawn by Andrew Mangiapane with 1:38 remaining in regulation. The Blackhawks did not win it there, but some of that power play bled into overtime. Although the Blackhawks were unable to win on the power play in overtime, they did once it returned to 3-on-3. Ryan Donato scored with a snipe, and his team skated off with a much-needed victory.
